title: What If Elephants Had Won? The Podcast That Imagines a World Where Rome Lost
summary: Imagine you're playing a video game, and you lose a big battle. You hit 'restart' and try a different path. That's kind of what a new podcast called 'Almost History' does—but with real ancient wars! The latest episode asks a huge 'what if': What if Carthage, not Rome, had won the Punic Wars over 2,000 years ago? You've probably heard of Rome and its mighty empire. But Carthage was a powerful city in North Africa that nearly beat Rome. Their general, Hannibal, did something crazy: he marched elephants over the snowy Alps to attack Rome! He won battle after battle and almost destroyed the Roman Republic. In the podcast, historian Eve MacDonald says Carthage had 'enormous resources' and the fight was much closer than we think. But she also says, 'the Romans were probably never going to go away'—they were just too stubborn. If Carthage had won, our world might look totally different. Maybe we'd speak a language based on Punic instead of Latin. Our laws, buildings, and even the food we eat could have roots in North Africa instead of Rome. MacDonald points out that we've lost many stories from Carthage and its neighbors, so we don't fully appreciate their influence. The podcast is like a time-travel adventure for your ears, exploring how one tiny change could rewrite everything. You can find it on Acast and other podcast apps. So, next time you're building a sandcastle, think: what if the tide didn't come in? History is full of moments like that.
why_it_matters: Thinking about 'what if' in history can make you curious about how your own choices might change your future, just like a video game restart.

background_read: Carthage was a powerful city in North Africa, located in what is now Tunisia.
The Punic Wars were three long wars fought between Rome and Carthage from 264 to 146 BC.
Hannibal Barca was a Carthaginian general famous for crossing the Alps with elephants to surprise the Romans.
